note: The two best free companions to this course, verified on 2026-09-29. The build puts this group at the top of the Resources tab and links the matching Sakubi lesson in block 6 of each lesson (content/readings.json). Links that point to file downloads of copyrighted books were deliberately left out.

group.title: Best free companions (start here)
group.note: Two community guides that fit this course well: Sakubi explains grammar in plain English, lesson by lesson; the DJT guide explains the method (grammar guide → spaced repetition → reading real Japanese). Every lesson of this course links the matching Sakubi lesson in block 6.

items.name: Sakubi — a free Japanese grammar guide
items.desc: A fast, no-nonsense grammar guide in English: 54 short lessons (from だ/です and particles to aspect, conditionals and keigo notes) plus intermissions on pronunciation.
items.how: After each lesson of this course, open the Sakubi link in block 6 and read that section as a second explanation — then come back and do the homework.

items.name: Sakubi · Part 1: Getting Started
items.desc: Sakubi's first 12 lessons: being, nouns, particles and case, の, movement particles, verbs, negation, past, the て-form, で/では, relative clauses, irregular verbs.
items.how: A good one-sitting overview once you finish Genki I Lesson 4, and again after Lesson 12.

items.name: DJT Guide to Japanese
items.desc: A short guide to HOW to learn Japanese: kana first, one grammar guide read through, a core vocabulary deck in Anki, then reading native material while mining new words.
items.how: Read it once now, and again when you finish Genki I — it is the roadmap for the 'after the course' phase.

items.name: DJT guide · Now what do I do to actually learn Japanese?
items.desc: The step-by-step plan at the heart of the DJT guide.
items.how: Compare it with this course's Guide tab: the course covers the grammar-guide step; the app covers spaced repetition.

items.name: DJT guide · Kanji approaches
items.desc: Kanji through vocabulary vs. isolated kanji (mnemonics, radicals): benefits and drawbacks of each.
items.how: Read it before lesson P-21 (Kanji for life), or whenever kanji start to feel slow.

items.name: DJT Resource Guide
items.desc: The DJT community's curated list of learning resources and tools (kana, kanji, vocabulary, grammar, practice, Anki, dictionaries, typing, mobile).
items.how: Use the sections below; skip anything that asks you to download copyrighted books.

items.name: DJT Resource Guide · Grammar
items.desc: Grammar references beyond the beginner stage.
items.how: When you reach the N3 Bridge and need a second reference for a point.

items.name: DJT Resource Guide · Practice (reading, listening, production)
items.desc: Where to find material for reading, watching and speaking practice.
items.how: Pick one item for the Immersion block of your daily routine.

items.name: DJT Resource Guide · Anki
items.desc: How the community sets up Anki, the spaced-repetition app, and which decks it uses.
items.how: Optional: the ヅオリンゴー app already does SRS for the Genki vocabulary; use Anki only for extra decks.

items.name: DJT Resource Guide · Dictionaries and typing Japanese
items.desc: Dictionaries, pop-up dictionaries and how to type Japanese on your computer.
items.how: Set up a Japanese keyboard now: typing your homework sentences is great practice.

items.name: DJT Kana
items.how: An alternative to the app's Kana Trail for a quick 5-minute warm-up.

items.name: DJT guide · Core 2k/6k vocabulary
items.desc: The DJT page about the Core 2k/6k frequency decks for Anki.
items.how: Optional, after Genki I: the first 2,000 words cover most of what you will meet in easy native material.

items.name: Visualizing Japanese Grammar (George Washington University)
items.desc: A video series recommended by the DJT guide, written and presented by a native Japanese linguist, that shows grammar visually.
items.how: Use it to refresh a point you already studied in the course.
